title: A time-order test finds no clear fractional spectral narrowing in 112 selected CHIME events
abstract: We test whether later fitted components have smaller fractional spectral widths in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, release 20251231. The main sample has 112 events from 56 catalog sources. Equal source weights give a last-to-first geometric width ratio of 0.969. The 95 percent source bootstrap interval is 0.889 to 1.054. Fifty events have narrower last components. Edge, fit quality, pulse separation and source controls give no clear mean change. Exact three-error curvature boxes leave changes in both directions. The result concerns fitted spectral shape in a selected sample. It does not prove a fixed spectrum or exclude a weak time trend. Shared fit errors, the beam response and component selection limit physical interpretation. Independent observations do not confirm this test. No new source or planet is found. The package has original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, input hashes and external retrieval steps.

display.caption: Source-balanced mean log width ratios and 95 percent source bootstrap intervals. Negative values mean narrower later fractional spectra. Intervals omit fit and instrument systematics.
